title: Add bounds checks before writing PID history arrays
description: `iRoastControl Software/PIDController.cs` writes `pidvalues[Convert.ToInt32(currentTime)]` in `Set()` and `Update()` without checking whether `currentTime` is within the 1200-sample array. Long roasts or unexpected timestamps can throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` and stop control updates mid-roast. Clamp or guard the index and define what should happen after the recorded profile length is exceeded.
result_text:
Implemented the PID history guard in [PIDController.cs](/home/smicbee/repos/orchestrator/data/repos/7ae06174-2103-45f0-ba52-3b54a558e76c/iRoastControl%20Software/PIDController.cs):25. `Set()` and `Update()` now write through `RecordPidValue()`, which rejects negative, NaN, infinite, and beyond-1200-sample timestamps before indexing `pidvalues`. After the recorded profile length is exceeded, PID output calculation continues and the history array is simply not updated.

Created the ticket summary at [result.md](/home/smicbee/repos/orchestrator/data/repos/7ae06174-2103-45f0-ba52-3b54a558e76c/tickets/36701760-8fb3-49de-bbbe-963350389d5f/result.md):1.

Verification: `xbuild 'iRoastControl Software/iRoastControl.sln' /p:Configuration=Debug /p:Platform="Any CPU"` succeeded. It produced existing project warnings only.

I attempted to commit with `Guard PID history recording bounds`, but the sandbox blocked writing `.git/index.lock` with `Read-only file system`, so the changes are not committed. The build also updated the tracked Debug executables under `iRoastControl Software/bin/Debug/` and `iRoastControl Software/obj/Debug/`.
